verdict_reason: The kernel is exact wherever the critical-point set is complete: against the AUTHORS' OWN Persistence Landscape Toolbox (Bubenik & Dlotko source.zip, compiled and executed locally) BLME agrees across 17 diagrams of 1-999 bars to a worst relative disagreement of 8.324e-16 on maxima, 4.735e-16 on integrals, 4.987e-16 on L2 norms and 5.202e-15 on the whole-landscape L1, and Bubenik Prop. 5 comes out three-way identical (paper 72 / toolbox 72.000000000000000 / BLME 72.000000000000000 for ||lambda||_1, and 6 / 6.000000000000000 / 6.000000000000000 for ||lambda||_inf, relative error 0.0). Round-4's blocking scale defect is FIXED and I verified it: with the pre-ripser rescale removed, cloud scales 1e-30/1e-25/1e20/1e38 return 0 finite H0 bars and every statistic 0.0, while the current code retains all 19 bars and reproduces the homogeneous values across 1e-30..1e38 to a worst 1.03e-07 (float32 eps 1.19e-07) AND stays bit-identical to the un-rescaled path on ordinary data (5/5 cases, xmax 3.3e-05..3.3e+05, prescale 1.0). NOT GREEN for one reason only: above _PAIRWISE_CAND_CAP=3000 the top-3000-by-persistence heuristic drops a locally active short bar, and on the valid 3001-bar diagram {1x[1,6], 4x[2,8], 4x[100+8j,107+8j] j=0..748} the toolbox gives lambda_5 max/integral/L2 = 2.000000000/4.000000/2.309401077 where BLME emits 1.500000000/3.500000/1.957890021 (-25.0%/-12.5%/-15.22%); in the same call _meta_landscape_quadrature='refined_lower_bound' is a false claim, because lambda_1's integral is 9187.000000 against the toolbox's 9186.500000 (+0.5) while lambda_5's is -0.5, i.e. the quadrature error is two-sided.
comparable_reason: The three exported statistics are homogeneous of degree 1, 3/2 and 2 in the diagram scale, hence in the representation scale, and I measured the exponents rather than inferring them: rescaling one fixed cloud by c = 0.25/2/7/10 multiplies landscape_max_1 by 0.250000/2.000000/7.000000/10.000001 (= c), landscape_norm_1 by 0.125000/2.828427/18.520260/31.622779 (= c^1.5) and mean_landscape_integral by 0.062500/4.000000/49.000001/100.000002 (= c^2). Purely in the diagram this is exact to 2.366e-16 across 1e-160 to 1e+150. Two models computing the SAME function under different residual-stream gauges therefore report different landscapes, and even two layers of one model are not comparable: on distilgpt2 layer_3_h0_landscape_max_1 = 6.158383846 against layer_5_h0 = 19.186538696 (3.1x) and mean_landscape_integral 31.565652917 against 309.640921168 (9.8x). runtime NORMALIZERS has exactly 0 entries and the end-to-end run emitted 0 normalized keys, so no comparable twin exists; the sibling topology_homology does divide by mean pairwise distance and this task does not.
github_repo: https://www2.math.upenn.edu/~dlotko/persistenceLandscape.html (source.zip, Bubenik & Dlotko Persistence Landscape Toolbox); cross-checked against scikit-tda/persim 0.3.8
github_reason: I fetched source.zip from Dlotko's toolbox page (linked from Bubenik's own software page at people.clas.ufl.edu/peterbubenik/software/), compiled the original C++ PersistenceLandscape.h/PersistenceBarcode.h with a 45-line driver (g++ -O2 -std=c++11), and ran it head-to-head with BLME on 17 shared diagrams (Fig. 3, the module's {[1,6],[2,8],[3,4]}, a 6-bar multi-bar case exercising k-selection at K=4, the narrow {[0,1000],[100,100.1]} case, random n=1..401, and all-equal-birth n=50/300/999 standing in for ripser H0). Worst relative disagreement: 8.324e-16 (maxima), 4.735e-16 (per-level integrals), 4.987e-16 (per-level L2 norms), 5.202e-15 (whole-landscape L1 via computeIntegralOfLandscape). Independently, persim 0.3.8 PersLandscapeExact agrees to a worst 2.697e-15 over 17 diagrams up to 4000 bars, with the multi-bar K=4 case at 0.000e+00/1.946e-16/0.000e+00 -- confirming task_metadata.py's '~9e-16' claim to the right order. The SAME toolbox also confirms the 3001-bar defect above (its lambda_5 = 2.000000000 vs BLME's 1.500000000).
paper_reason: Bubenik 2015 (JMLR 16:77-102) Prop. 5 gives ||lambda||_1 = (1/4) sum_i (d_i-b_i)^2 and ||lambda||_inf = (1/2) max_i (d_i-b_i); I re-derived both (a single bar's tent has base d-b and height (d-b)/2, so its integral is (d-b)^2/4, and summing all order statistics equals summing all tents) rather than taking them second-hand. On the Fig. 3 rescaled diagram (midpoint, half-persistence) = (6,6),(10,6), i.e. bars [0,12] and [4,16], BLME returns integrals [56.0, 16.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0] summing to 72.000000000000000 against the published 72, and landscape_max_1 = 6.000000000000000 against 6 -- both relative error 0.00e+00, and both matched by the authors' toolbox to 0.00e+00. Prop. 5 also holds on 5 random diagrams with K set to the bar count (n = 3..120): worst relative error 3.0e-16 for L1 and 1.8e-16 for the sup norm. Analytic single-bar anchors are exact too: (2,9) gives L1 12.250000000000000 = (d-b)^2/4 (rel 0.0), max 3.500000000000000 = (d-b)/2 (rel 0.0), L2 5.346338310781813 = (d-b)^1.5/sqrt(12) (rel 1.661e-16).
confounds_reason: The confound is representation SCALE, and it is total -- but it is NOT a mechanical width or depth count, which is the distinction that matters. Isometric zero-padding of one fixed 20-point cloud from d = 8 to d = 16/64/256/1024/4096 leaves landscape_max_1, landscape_norm_1 and mean_landscape_integral unchanged at |diff| 0.00e+00 in all five cases (1.581521511077881 / 1.623928955212760 / 2.161559528398817), because an isometry preserves pairwise distances and hence the diagram. Rescaling the same cloud instead moves the three outputs by exactly c^1 / c^1.5 / c^2 (measured 7.000000 / 18.520260 / 49.000001 at c = 7), so any function-preserving gauge change on the residual stream moves every reported value while leaving the model's outputs alone. d_model and n_layers enter only through whatever activation norm the architecture happens to have.
defects: CODE/FIDELITY, src/blme/tasks/topology/persistence_landscape.py:186-201: above _PAIRWISE_CAND_CAP=3000 the pairwise-intersection set is built from the 3000 MOST PERSISTENT bars, which is not a valid restriction -- a shorter bar can be locally active in the top K where the long bars have disjoint support. On {1x[1,6], 4x[2,8], 4x[100+8j,107+8j] j=0..748} (3001 bars) the authors' own toolbox gives lambda_5 max/integral/L2 = 2.000000000/4.000000/2.309401077 and BLME emits 1.500000000/3.500000/1.957890021 (-25.0%/-12.5%/-15.22%). The missing candidate is exactly t = (b_[2,8] + d_[1,6])/2 = 4.0, dropped because [1,6] has the smallest persistence of the 3001.

CODE/OUTPUT, persistence_landscape.py:260: _meta_landscape_quadrature = 'refined_lower_bound' asserts one-sidedness that is measurably false. On the same 3001-bar call the signed integral errors against the toolbox are +0.500000 for lambda_1 (9187.000000 vs 9186.500000) and -0.500000 for lambda_5: omitting a breakpoint that is a local maximum under-estimates, omitting one that is a local minimum over-estimates, so both signs occur. _meta_landscape_max_status = 'lower_bound' IS correct, because every candidate and grid point is a genuine evaluation of lambda_k.

NOT REACHABLE AT ANY PLAUSIBLE CONFIG, and this is why it does not change the study's numbers: I measured ripser's finite bar counts at N = 20/100/400/1000 as H0 = 19/99/399/999 with ALL births exactly 0.0 in every case, so the _all_same_birth exception keeps H0 on the exact path at any size (verified against persim at n = 3001 and n = 4000, relative error 1.4e-16). H1 = 6/109/821/2442 over the same sweep, so at the shipped num_samples = 20 the diagram has 6 H1 bars against a 3000 cap, and even at num_samples = 1000 -- the value topology_betti_curve and topology_persistence_entropy were raised to -- it is 2442, still below the cap. A live distilgpt2 run reports _meta_landscape_max_status = 'exact' and _meta_landscape_quadrature = 'exact' on all six emitted keys, with _meta_landscape_n_bars = 19 (H0) and 4 (H1).

CODE/RESOURCE, persistence_landscape.py:182-206: the cap bounds the n^2 candidate VECTOR but the code then materialises dense (n_bars, n_candidates) arrays. A generic n = 1000 diagram yields ~1,002,000 unique candidates, so one such array is ~8.0 GB and the four (left_c, right_c, tents_c, srt) ~32 GB; at n = 3000 that is ~216 GB and ~865 GB. Harmless at 19 bars / 399 candidates, but it bites before the cap does if num_samples is ever raised.

NAMING, persistence_landscape.py:299,417-418: mean_landscape_integral is the mean over the configured first K levels, not Bubenik's whole-landscape L1 norm. On the fixed diagram {[1,6],[2,8],[3,4]} it reads 5.166667/3.100000/1.550000 at K = 3/5/10 while the exact total stays 15.500000, so the key is K-dependent by construction -- and Prop. 5 gives the K-free total, sum_i (d_i-b_i)^2/4, in closed form for free.

MINOR/NUMERICS, persistence_landscape.py:387-391: the pre-ripser divisor is float(np.max(np.abs(X))), not a power of two, so inside the rescaled regime it perturbs the float32 coordinates by up to ~6e-08 relative (measured worst end-to-end deviation 1.03e-07 across 1e-30..1e38, i.e. at the float32 floor). The comment claiming it 'only shifts exponents' is therefore not literally true; using 2.0 ** round(log2(xmax)) would make it exact. The CONDITIONAL guard itself is right and I verified it: outside the fire band the path is bit-identical to the un-rescaled one in 5/5 cases.

CONFIG (separate from the implementation axis), defaults.yaml:161-164: the merged config is exactly num_samples = 20, n_landscapes = 5, n_points = 200, and max_length = 128 is hard-coded at persistence_landscape.py:356 rather than configurable. H1 carries 4 bars on a live distilgpt2 run. The two sibling topology tasks were raised to num_samples = 1000 and this one was not.

TEST COVERAGE: tests/test_scale_invariance.py passes 11/11 and the three checked-in landscape parity tests pass, but none of them exercises _landscape_stats above the 3000-bar cap, and the 3001-bar -25.0% case is unpinned. The pre-ripser rescale, which is the fix that closed the round-4 blocker, also has no regression in tests/test_scale_invariance.py despite being exactly that file's defect class.
fix: 1) Replace the top-3000-by-persistence heuristic with an exact critical-pair sweep (or a chunked one that does not materialise (n_bars, n_candidates)), or fail closed above the exact limit; the current selection provably misses locally active short bars, costing lambda_5 -25.0% on the 3001-bar case. 2) Rename _meta_landscape_quadrature's 'refined_lower_bound' to 'refined_approximation' -- the measured errors are +0.5 and -0.5 in the same call, so it is not a bound in either direction. 3) Add regressions for the 3001-bar locally-active-short-bar construction and, more importantly, for the pre-ripser rescale in tests/test_scale_invariance.py: without it cloud scales 1e-30/1e-25/1e20/1e38 return 0 bars and all-zero statistics. 4) Optional but free: make the pre-ripser divisor a power of two (2.0 ** round(log2(xmax))) so the rescaled regime is exact rather than float32-exact, and correct the 'only shifts exponents' comment. 5) Emit the K-free Prop. 5 total sum_i (d_i-b_i)^2/4 alongside mean_landscape_integral, or rename the latter to make its K-dependence explicit. 6) Config, not implementation: raise num_samples from 20 to 1000 for consistency with topology_betti_curve and topology_persistence_entropy (still safely below the cap at 2442 H1 bars), expose max_length, and register a scale-normalised twin (divide max / norm / integral by mean pairwise distance to powers 1 / 1.5 / 2 -- the exact homogeneity degrees measured here) before any cross-model comparison is attempted.
